problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,y,\,4x⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=4$ for $0\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 3.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$

feedback.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨yz,\,xz,\,xy⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=4$ for $-1\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 2.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the upward-pointing unit normal vector $n.$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For the surface $z=4$ for  $-1\le x\le 1$ and $0\le y\le 2,$ the upward-pointing unit normal vector is

$$
n=⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=4$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨yz,\,xz,\,xy⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨4y,\,4x,\,xy⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =xy.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}xy\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}x\,\text{d}x\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2}y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{-1}^{1}\cdot {\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =0\cdot 2 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
